{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development, Hosting and Revenue-Share Agreement with HDI)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer/Company side) 
**Scope:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 against 18 rules. All statements below are drawn from the verified findings; no additional section references or conclusions have been added.

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. Seven rules are met (or sit at the fallback and are therefore acceptable without redline), five clauses are missing entirely, and six clauses deviate on material terms.

The dominant theme is **absence of core protections rather than bad drafting**: the Agreement has no limitation of liability, no indemnity (including no IP-infringement indemnity from HDI), no IP ownership or assignment provision, no insurance covenant, no HDI performance warranty, and no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates our customer-facing Site and holds our Content, user information and data, so each of these gaps sits directly on our risk.

The principal commercial deviation is the **Termination Payment in § 4.2(a)** — one-half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable on any Company termination, including for HDI's own breach, and one-way (§ 4.2(b) relieves HDI of any reciprocal payment). It scales without limit as the Site succeeds and materially exceeds the fallback cap of three months' fees. It is flagged under both the termination-for-convenience and liquidated-damages rules because both rules are independently breached.

Several items are in our favour and are not being reopened: the § 3.1 revenue share applies only above an $11,000 monthly floor with no minimum commitment; there is no MFN and no non-solicit binding us; § 6.3 restrains HDI for the term plus two years; there is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer; and § 3.4 already has HDI bearing its own inspection costs.

**Verification caveat:** two findings (Termination for convenience; Audit rights) carry a failed verification status and must be re-checked against the executed text before the redline is issued. Nine further findings were repaired during verification and should be spot-checked on the same pass.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Verification | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 (Warranties block, § 9) | Repaired | § 9 covers only corporate existence, authority, enforceability, no-conflict and the Globix acknowledgement. No workmanlike-performance, conformance, compliance-with-law or no-malicious-code warranty and no warranty remedy; § 1.6 go-live right is not a conformance warranty. Fails the fallback. Inserting preferred warranty as new § 9(c). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant (fallback) | § 5.4 (restriction at § 6.1) | Pass | Term-only, no post-term tail; one-year term terminable on 90 days' notice; scope limited to a single online channel for defined "Deerskin Products" plus named competitors, with § 6.2 closeout carve-out. Missing internal-development/acquisition carve-out noted only. |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 5.4 | Repaired | No ownership or assignment provision anywhere; § 5.2 gives editorial control only, § 8 confidentiality only, § 10.2 does not address IP. Proposed new § 5.5 confirming our ownership of Content, Site, deliverables and Site data, HDI retaining pre-existing IP with licence back, no joint ownership. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 | Repaired | No cap, no consequential-damages exclusion anywhere. Proposing mutual cap at greater of 12 months' § 3 fees and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP uncapped, and our § 3 / § 4.2 payment obligations excluded. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 (term/termination at §§ 4.1–4.2) | **Fail — re-verify** | 90-day mutual convenience right sits at the fallback; the failure is the § 4.2(a) exit penalty (one-half of trailing 12-month Net Sales above $800,000), one-way and payable even on termination for HDI's breach. Redline caps at three months' § 3.1 fees and disapplies where we terminate under § 1.6 or for HDI's breach. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 (§ 10.5) | Pass | New York law, conflicts disapplied; no arbitration and no foreign seat. Absence of an express exclusive New York County venue designation noted only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 1.4 | Pass | No parity or price-matching language in either direction; economics are the flat § 3 revenue share. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 1.4 | Pass | No minimum, guaranteed volume or take-or-pay; § 3.1 revenue share applies only above the $11,000 monthly floor. § 4.2 Termination Payment assessed under the termination/LD rules, not double-flagged. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | Pass | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binds us; only the § 10.2 independent-contractor language. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 | Repaired | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; no IP-infringement indemnity from the party that builds, hosts and operates the Site. Inserting preferred vendor indemnity as new § 9(c) with notice/control/cooperation and a carve-out for Company-supplied Content. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | Repaired | No insurance provision; HDI hosts the Site and holds our user information and data. Inserting new § 10.9 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback noted in comment. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 6.1) | Repaired | Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit (§ 1.6 covers only a missed initial launch; any other exit triggers the Termination Payment). Taking the fallback given reciprocity in § 6.3: confine to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months, automatic end on HDI launch or service failure. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 4.2(a)) | Repaired | Customer-payable stipulated sum that exceeds three months' § 3.1 fees once annual Net Sales pass roughly $0.9m, and is payable even on termination for HDI's breach. Cap at three months' fees (average monthly § 3.1 payments over the preceding 12 months); deletion offered as the preferred alternative. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | Repaired | The only inbound grant runs to "the Company" alone, with no affiliate or contractor coverage and no mechanism to add them — short of the fallback. Redline extends § 1.4 to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirms non-revocability during the term and successor transfer. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 4.1) | Repaired | Evergreen one-year renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal notice exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Moving to 30 days (60 acceptable). No renewal uplift language, so the price-cap point is not engaged; absence of a vendor reminder noted only. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 | Repaired | § 4 covers only notice, Termination Date and the Termination Payment; nothing in §§ 4, 8 or 10.7 requires transition help or return of our Content and Site user data. Inserting new § 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (§ 10.3) | Repaired | § 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause with no consent standard, so HDI could transfer this hosting engagement — and access to our confidential data and customer-facing Site — to a competitor without our consent. Redline confirms our affiliate/successor carve-out and conditions HDI assignment on our consent, not unreasonably withheld, never to a competitor. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (§ 3.4) | **Fail — re-verify** | Notice, business-hours and cost terms meet or beat preferred, and scope is limited to the General Manager's payment-calculation records, but there is no frequency limit. Minimal edit inserts a once-per-twelve-month cap; independent-auditor and confidentiality points noted, § 8.2 already binding HDI. |

## Walk-away items

The following findings were assessed as walk-away territory under the applicable rules and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No HDI indemnity of any kind (INDEMN — missing).** HDI builds, hosts and operates the Site and supplies the software and Content administration tools under §§ 1.1–1.4; the total absence of an IP-infringement indemnity is walk-away under the rule and fails the fallback.
2. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE — missing).** HDI hosts the Site on its own server and holds our Content, user information and data (§§ 1.1–1.3, 8.1) — the playbook's walk-away scenario of an uninsured vendor handling personal data.
3. **Full-term exclusivity with no performance exit (EXCLUSIVITY — § 6.1).** Exclusive dealing for an auto-renewing term with no exit tied to HDI's performance is walk-away territory; we are proposing the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic end on service or delivery failure) rather than deletion, in recognition of the reciprocal restraint on HDI in § 6.3.
4. **Unlimited inspection frequency (AUDIT — § 3.4).** The rule treats unlimited audits as walk-away territory; the once-per-twelve-month cap is the minimal cure. Subject to re-verification.

Also to be resolved before signature, though not classified as walk-away: the **§ 4.2(a) Termination Payment**, which is one-way, uncapped in growth, and bites even where we terminate for HDI's failure.

## Next steps

1. **Re-verify the two failed findings** (T4C / § 4.2 exit penalty and AUDIT / § 3.4 frequency) against the executed text before the markup leaves our side; spot-check the nine repaired findings on the same pass.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and five missing clauses: new § 9(c) (performance warranty and vendor indemnity), new § 5.5 (ownership), new § 4.3 (transition and data return), new § 10.9 (insurance), a mutual limitation of liability, the § 4.2 Termination Payment cap and carve-out, § 6.1 exclusivity limits, § 1.4 affiliate/contractor licence coverage, § 4.1 non-renewal notice at 30 days, § 10.3 assignment consent, and the § 3.4 frequency cap.
3. **Sequence the negotiation** around the four walk-away items plus the Termination Payment; treat renewal notice, licence scope, assignment and audit frequency as a single clean-up package we can close quickly.
4. **Pre-agree our fallbacks** so we can settle at pace: 12 months' fees / USD 1M on the liability cap; E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M on insurance; 60 days on non-renewal notice; 90 days' software / 30 days' services on warranty; affiliates on written notice on the licence grant.
5. **Flag for the business** that HDI bears all design, development, hosting and maintenance cost under §§ 1.2–1.3 and is paid solely from revenue share. That bargain is why we are proposing to cap rather than delete the exit fee and to take the fallback on exclusivity; please confirm that trade-off before we send.
6. **Note the items we are not reopening** (no MFN, no minimum commitment, no non-solicit, New York law, § 6.3 restraint on HDI, HDI-borne inspection costs) so they are not conceded in a later round."}
